experiment: Does naive offline-to-online IQLD fine-tuning fall into an unlearning trough (Cal-QL/OVMSE prediction)?
design: from v11 best_safe, 180 ep, guard-in-loop. A: expert_fraction 1.0->0.5 (online data truly in batch, confirmed actual 0.5). B: expert_fraction 1.0 (pure offline control). Formal 5x100 eval of best_safe each.
conclusion: CONFIRMED: naive online fine-tuning (A) is WORSE than pure offline continuation (B): nominal 0.890 vs 0.904, robust 0.880 vs 0.892. Introducing online data WITHOUT anti-unlearning mechanisms degrades the pretrained policy - the Cal-QL/OVMSE 'unlearning trough'. 180 episodes is NOT enough to exit the trough (A stays below its start). Reproduces the user's earlier 200-ep drop (0.908->0.892). B (offline-only) also does not improve (consistent with rho 0.80->0.88 not transferring). Remedy per literature: Cal-QL calibration or OVMSE offline-value-memory (target=max(offline memory, online TD)) + sequential exploration; plain expert_fraction annealing is insufficient.
